Statins appear to have effects on bone metabo- lism and preliminary studies1,2 have suggested that some statins may increase bone mineral density. However, the clinical rele- vance of any effect is unclear.3 Several case-control studies4-6 have also suggested that use of statins may protect against frac- tures, but another case-control study7 and an observational study8 failed to support such an association. A review9 of 4 fur- ther observational studies found that the risk of fracture was low- er in women taking statins, but analysis of data from randomised studies of statins for cardiovascular disease10,11 failed to confirm any effect, and controlled studies are needed3,12 to confirm the role of statins in the management of osteoporosis (p.1084). 1.
